entities.name: Owain Goch ap Gruffydd
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Owain Goch ap Gruffydd was the younger brother of the legendary Welsh princes Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and Dafydd ap Gruffudd, and for a brief period in the late 1240s and early 1250s, he ruled over part of the Kingdom of Gwynedd.

This fleeting reign was a consequence of the complex power struggles in medieval Wales, where the fragmented kingdoms were constantly vying for control. Owain's short tenure as ruler was marked by a series of battles against his rivals, including the English monarchy.

Despite his brief time in power, Owain's legacy as a leader and a symbol of Welsh resistance against English rule has endured for centuries.

As he died in 1282, Owain's story became part of the larger narrative of the decline of the Welsh kingdoms and the rise of English dominance in Wales.

The significance of Owain's story lies in its role in shaping the cultural and historical identity of Wales, a nation that has struggled to maintain its distinctiveness in the face of overwhelming external forces.
